svg.title: Kubernetes event-driven architecture
svg.desc: Event-driven architecture of the Kubernetes control plane: kube-apiserver as central event broker; kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, and kube-proxy as independent event consumers watching resource change events via shared informers. No component directly calls another.

g.onclick: sendPrompt('Who submits resource changes to the Kubernetes API server?')
sendPrompt('How does kube-apiserver act as the central event broker?')
g.text: All resource changes stored in etcd · emits watch stream to all consumers

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How does the Deployment controller react to events?')
sendPrompt('How does the ReplicaSet controller react to events?')
sendPrompt('How does the Job controller react to events?')
sendPrompt('How does the DaemonSet controller react to events?')
sendPrompt('How does the GarbageCollector controller work?')
sendPrompt('How does the SchedulingQueue consume Pod events?')
sendPrompt('How does the scheduler filter and score nodes?')
sendPrompt('How does the scheduler bind a Pod to a node?')

g.text: Watches Pod events on its node

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What is the Pod Lifecycle Event Generator (PLEG)?')
sendPrompt('What does SyncPod do in kubelet?')
sendPrompt('How does kube-proxy watch Service and EndpointSlice events?')
g.text: Watches Service + EndpointSlice change events · reprograms iptables / nftables rules

svg.text: write status / binding back to API server

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How does etcd store Kubernetes state?')
g.text: Persistent store for all resource objects

svg.text: No component directly calls another — all coordination mediated through the API server watch stream
